title: A quasi-coherent module on a qcqs scheme is a filtered colimit of modules of finite presentation, indexed by a filtered category (Stacks 01PJ)
statement: Let $X$ be a scheme [def-pc-scheme] which is quasi-compact [def-weil-pbc-quasi-compact-scheme] and quasi-separated [def-weil-quasi-separated-morphism], and let $\mathcal F$ be a quasi-coherent $\mathcal O_X$-module [pqf-def-coherent], [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category]. An $\mathcal O_X$-module $\mathcal G$ is *of finite presentation* if every point of $X$ has an open neighbourhood $U$ with an exact sequence $\mathcal O_U^{\oplus m}\to\mathcal O_U^{\oplus n}\to\mathcal G|_U\to0$ of $\mathcal O_U$-modules [def-weil-pbc-module-finite-type-presentation] (Stacks, Modules, Definition 01BN). Then there exist a small filtered category $\mathcal I$ (its objects form a set; it is nonempty, any two objects $i,i'$ admit morphisms $i\to i''$, $i'\to i''$ to a common object, and any two parallel morphisms $a,b:i\to i'$ are equalized by some $c:i'\to i''$, $ca=cb$) [def-weil-pbc-category-colimit], a functor $M:\mathcal I\to\Mod(\mathcal O_X)$, $i\mapsto\mathcal F_i$, with every $\mathcal F_i$ of finite presentation, and $\mathcal O_X$-module maps $\varphi_i:\mathcal F_i\to\mathcal F$ with $\varphi_{i'}\circ M(a)=\varphi_i$ for every morphism $a:i\to i'$ of $\mathcal I$, such that $(\mathcal F,(\varphi_i)_i)$ is a colimit of $M$ in the category of $\mathcal O_X$-modules [def-weil-pbc-category-colimit].

source.place: Properties, Lemma 01PJ (lemma-directed-colimit-diagram-finite-presentation, line 3040); its proof uses Modules, Lemma 01BC (lemma-set-isomorphism-classes-finite-type-modules), direct sums and cokernels of finitely presented modules, stalks of colimits (Sheaves, Section 009E), Properties, Lemma 01PF (lemma-extend, line 2847) and Lemma 01PI (lemma-extend-finite-presentation, line 2924)

proof.text: Apply the finitely presented pairs lemma to $X,\mathcal F$. It supplies a small filtered category $\mathcal I$, a diagram $M(i)=\mathcal F_i$ of finitely presented modules, and a cocone $(\varphi_i)$ to $\mathcal F$. Every finitely presented pair over $\mathcal F$ is represented up to an isomorphism over $\mathcal F$, and arrows are all module maps commuting with those maps to $\mathcal F$.

source.place: Lemma 01PJ, choice of pairs and filteredness, lines 3066-3120

proof.text: Mathlib supplies all small colimits in X.Modules. Form L = colim M, with comparison φ : L → F from the canonical cocone. By the module-stalk filtered-colimit lemma, the stalk cocone of L is a colimit of the diagram of module stalks. The elementwise filtered-module-colimit lemma therefore represents each element of L_x by a germ at a stage.

source.place: Lemma 01PJ, stalk comparison; Modules 01AH; Modules on Sites 03DB

proof.text: For a stage germ $s\in(\mathcal F_i)_x$ with $(\varphi_i)_x(s)=0$, kernel-germ effacement gives a finitely presented quotient $q:\mathcal F_i\to\mathcal Q$ and $\beta:\mathcal Q\to\mathcal F$ with $\beta q=\varphi_i$ and $q_x(s)=0$. Choose its representative $e:\mathcal F_j\xrightarrow{\sim}\mathcal Q$, with $\beta e=\varphi_j$. Then $e^{-1}q:i\to j$ is an arrow killing $s$. Every element of $L_x$ has a stage representative, so zero detection in the filtered colimit proves $\varphi_x$ injective.

For $s\in\mathcal F_x$, the germ-lifting lemma gives a finitely presented $\mathcal G$, a map $\psi:\mathcal G\to\mathcal F$ and $t\in\mathcal G_x$ with $\psi_x(t)=s$. Choose its representative $e:\mathcal F_i\xrightarrow{\sim}\mathcal G$, with $\psi e=\varphi_i$. The germ $(e^{-1})_x(t)$ represents an element of $L_x$ whose image under $\varphi_x$ is $s$. Thus $\varphi_x$ is surjective.

Stalkwise detection makes $\varphi$ invertible. For any cocone $(\mu_i)$ to $N$, let $h:L\to N$ be its unique colimit factor. Then $h\varphi^{-1}$ factors $(\mu_i)$ through $\mathcal F$. Any other factor $g$ satisfies $g\varphi=h$ by uniqueness for $L$, hence equals $h\varphi^{-1}$. This proves the required colimit property.
